title: Why do planets go round the Sun?
examples: Does the Sun pull the planets with a rope?
What keeps the Earth from flying away from the Sun?
Is it like a giant spinning merry-go-round?

explain.say: The Sun has a strong pull called gravity. Gravity pulls things towards each other.

draw.text: Why do planets go round the Sun?

explain.say: Gravity is a pull you cannot see. Bigger things have a stronger pull.
The planets are moving very fast. They would keep going in a straight line.
The Sun's gravity pulls them in, while their speed carries them sideways. So they go round in a loop.
Think of swinging a ball on a string. The string pulls the ball in, so it goes round you.

draw.text: Swinging a ball on a string.

explain.say: If you let go, the ball flies off in a straight line.

draw.text: Swinging a ball in a circle.

faq.q: Does the Sun pull the planets with a rope?
faq.a: No, it is not like a real rope. Gravity is an invisible force that pulls things together.
asks: Does the Sun use a string to pull us?

faq.q: Why don't the planets just fall into the Sun?
faq.a: They are moving sideways very fast. This sideways push keeps them from falling straight in.
asks: If gravity pulls, why don't they crash?
What stops them from falling in?

faq.q: Is the pull the same for all planets?
faq.a: No, the pull is stronger for bigger things. The Sun is much bigger than any planet.
asks: Does Jupiter feel the pull more than Earth?
Is the pull stronger close to the Sun?

faq.q: Does the Earth pull the Sun?
faq.a: Yes, a tiny bit. The Sun is so much bigger that its pull on the Earth is the one we notice.

faq.q: Is orbiting the same as spinning?
faq.a: Spinning is going around an axis, like a top. Orbiting is going around another big object, like the Sun.
asks: What is the difference between spinning and orbiting?
Can something spin and orbit at the same time?

facts: Gravity is the force that pulls objects with mass together.
Planets orbit the Sun because of gravity and their forward speed.
The Sun has the strongest gravity in our solar system.
Planets closer to the Sun move faster than planets far away.

quiz.say: What pulls the planets towards the Sun?
quiz.why: Gravity is the pull between the Sun and the planets.

wrong.0: Magnets pull some metals, and gravity pulls everything.
wrong.2: Sunlight gives light and heat, and gravity does the pulling.

quiz.say: You swing a ball on a string and let go. Where does the ball go?
quiz.why: Without the pull of the string, the ball flies off in a straight line.

wrong.1: Nothing pulls it back once you let go.
wrong.2: The string made it go round, and now the string is gone.

quiz.say: What two things keep a planet going round the Sun?
quiz.why: Gravity pulls the planet in, and its speed carries it sideways. Together they make an orbit.

wrong.0: Sunlight and heat warm the planets, but they make no orbit.
wrong.1: Gravity alone would pull the planet into the Sun, so speed is needed too.
